title.en: The genitive plural: the hard one, made logical

card: Needed after **мно́го**, **ско́лько**, **нет** and numbers from 5. Three endings: **-ов/-ев** for most masculine nouns (**столо́в**, **музе́ев**), **-ей** for nouns ending in **-ь** or **ж, ш, щ, ч** (**двере́й**, **враче́й**), and **no ending** for feminine **-а** and neuter **-о** nouns (**книг**, **слов**), often with a vowel slipped in (**ру́чка → ру́чек**).

sections.body: The genitive plural is famous for being irregular, but it follows a neat logic: **the ending "swaps" with the nominative singular.** Nouns that have *no* ending in the singular (**стол**) get a real ending in the genitive plural (**столо́в**); nouns that *have* an ending in the singular (**кни́га**, **сло́во**) lose it (**книг**, **слов**). It's as if Russian keeps one ending per word between these two forms.

sections.title: Fleeting vowels
sections.body: When the zero ending would leave two consonants jammed together at the end of the word, Russian slips in an **о** or **е** to make it pronounceable: **ру́чка → ру́чек**, **окно́ → о́кон**, **де́вушка → де́вушек**, **письмо́ → пи́сем**. The vowel is **о** after a hard consonant (**о́кон**) and usually **е** after a soft one or after **ж, ш, ч** (**ру́чек**, **де́вушек**).

sections.title: Irregulars worth learning now
sections.body:
- **челове́к → люде́й** (but **пять челове́к** after numbers)
- **ребёнок → дете́й**
- **год → лет** (after numbers and **мно́го**)
- **друг → друзе́й**, **брат → бра́тьев**, **стул → сту́льев**
- **раз → раз** (**мно́го раз**), **глаз → глаз**, **солда́т → солда́т**
- **день → дней**, **де́ньги → де́нег**
**The swap rule**: if the dictionary form ends in a consonant, the genitive plural has an ending; if it ends in a vowel, the genitive plural has none. *Something in one, nothing in the other.*

mistakes.why: Feminine **-а** nouns take the zero ending: **книг**.
After 5 and up: genitive plural, with a fleeting **е**.

examples.en: There are lots of books in the library.
How many children do you have?
We haven't seen each other for five years.
There were a lot of people there.
He has a lot of friends.
